title: Continuous limit of the square well problem in quantum mechanics
authors: Matheus D. Moro, Thiago T. Tsutsui, Antonio S. M. de Castro, Fabiano M. Andrade
abstract: The free-particle and square-well potentials are two of the most emblematic problems in quantum mechanics, illustrating essential concepts such as matter waves, energy quantization, and bound states. It is therefore natural to consider how the free-particle solutions emerge from the square well as the width approaches infinity. In this work, we present a systematic procedure to demonstrate this transition by applying a Fourier transform to the wave equation.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that the free-particle solution can be derived from the bound state solutions of the finite square well by taking the width to infinity. It uses Fourier transforms to map the discrete energy spectrum onto a continuous one, showing the mathematical consistency between confined and unconfined quantum systems.
main_problem: The work systematically demonstrates the mathematical transition from the discrete, quantized energy spectrum of a finite square well to the continuous spectrum characteristic of a free particle.
main_result: By applying Fourier analysis and taking the limit where the confining width approaches infinity, the bound state solutions correctly recover the plane-wave form of the free particle wave function.
method: The core method involves solving the time-independent Schrödinger equation for both finite and infinite wells, followed by mapping the resulting discrete summation structure onto a continuous integral representation using Fourier transform techniques.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum particle confined by a potential $U(x)$, comparing the free particle case to the finite and infinite square well potentials. The governing equation is the time-independent Schrödinger equation.
key_observables: Energy spectrum ($E$): transitioning from discrete eigenvalues ($E_n$) to a continuous band; wave functions ($\psi$).
important_parameters: Well width ($L$), potential height ($U_0$), and the limit $L 	o \infty$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on treating the transition from a discrete sum (Fourier Series) to a continuous integral (Fourier Transform), which requires careful handling of limits.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the potential profiles for finite and infinite wells. Figure 2 illustrates how the energy level spacing ($\Delta E$) decreases as $L$ increases, leading toward the continuum limit.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing solutions for the free particle (continuous spectrum), then solving the finite square well problem (discrete spectrum), and finally executing the mathematical procedure to show that the continuous limit of the discrete solutions yields the free-particle plane wave.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental, rigorous demonstration of how continuum limits are handled in quantum mechanics, which is crucial for understanding effective Hamiltonians or open system approximations where boundaries become negligible.
